newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt bank yields to French bank in joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Egypt bank yields to French bank in joint venture.

text.p: State-owned National Bank of Egypt (NBE) sold Credit Commercial de France (CCF) a large stake in their Egyptian joint venture in a deal worth 26.26 million pounds ($7.7 million) on Thursday, brokers said.

Bankers had expected NBE to sell CCF 16 percent of the joint venture, Credit International d'Egypte (CIE), giving CCF majority control, but it was not immediately clear if CCF had crossed the 50 percent threshold.
CCF previously owned 39 percent of CIE and on Thursday it bought 82,455 shares from NBE at 318.50 pounds a share, the brokers said. They did not know how many CIE shares exist.
NBE held 31 percent of CIE, BHF Bank of Germany holds 10 percent and employees of NBE and CIE have the other 20 percent.
The deal is in line with a broad trend towards foreign partners taking control of joint-venture banks with Egyptian state banks, under an amendment to the banking law this year.
Under the old regulations, the foreign partners could not own more than 49 percent of the equity in the joint ventures.
Earlier this month Societe Generale of France took majority control of its joint venture with NBE, known as National Societe Generale Bank.

Egyptian American Bank has gone majority private-sector through a public share issue which diluted the stake of the state's Bank of Alexandria. The foreign partner is American Express Bank of the United States.
Other foreign banks are expected to follow the lead of CCF and Societe Generale as soon as they can reach agreement with their Egyptian public-sector partners.
